summary: The 5-agent Opus counsel: 4 staff Swift/AR reviewers (adversarial end-to-end review + industrial-standard test cases) + 1 industry researcher (industrial solutions to the critiques)

soundAreas: ARP-3 latch is genuinely fixed: GeoARSessionManager.swift:2095-2107 now derives `farMode`/`semanticMatteArmed` on every tick under `if semanticPass != nil`, with `geospatial.semanticActive` demoted to one of the AND-ed inputs, so the flag falls when semantics switch off and the Metal pass detaches (the ADR-035 heat regression path is closed).

SWE-6 negative cache is correctly ordered: DropEntityFactory.swift:121 and :142 insert into `failedAssets` BEFORE `onAssetLoaded?(name, false)` fires, and animatedModel checks `failedAssets` (line 218) ahead of the `requestAsset` call (line 222) — the rebuild -> re-request -> re-decode loop cannot re-arm. decodeTemplate now logs the Combine `.failure` (line 88-90).

SWE-8 actor conversion is sound: LocalDropStore is an actor (DropStore.swift:40) so load-modify-write in save/delete is serialized by construction; `testConcurrentSavesAllSurvive` (DropStoreTests.swift:109-130) pins the lost-write class it was meant to kill.

SWE-9 per-row decode is well-constructed: FailableDrop (DropStore.swift:65-81) refuses to mint a UUID for an id-less row, so a quarantined row can never be silently duplicated on disk; the SHA256-digest sidecar naming (DropStore.swift:122-129) is genuinely idempotent per distinct content and the timestamped `.corrupt-` quarantine no longer overwrites the previous backup.

PBS-4 acked-write continuations are leak-free in both places: FirebaseDropStore.swift:76-90 and AccountService.swift:99-116 resume exactly once on the completion path and once on the encode-throw path — no double-resume, no path where the continuation is abandoned.

PBS-7 seeding guard is correct: AccountService.swift:46 turns on `includeMetadataChanges`, :58-60 requires `!snapshot.exists && !metadata.isFromCache && profile == nil`, and :49-57 refuses to seed over an existing-but-undecodable document. The reinstall-overwrites-real-profile path is closed.

SWE-3 reconcile direction is right: reconcileCloud (DropStore.swift:317-327) only ever pushes and never clears, so absence from the in-memory array can no longer wipe the persisted outbox on a launch where auth resolves before the first load.

C26 delete ordering is right: remove() (DropStore.swift:290-301) destroys sync bookkeeping only after `local.delete` returns successfully; on failure the drop, the pending flag and the generation are all left intact and the error is both published and thrown.

C12 banner restructure works: DropsListScreen.swift:15-18 puts `banners` above the empty/list split, so a fully emptied library still renders the failure banners alongside 'No drops yet' (when the underlying flags are actually set — see findings 2 and 3).

findings.claim: The terminal `ownedByAnotherAccount` branch clears the pending flag for a write the server never accepted, and the only remaining signal (`lastSyncError`) is wiped by the next successful cloud read or the next successful write of any other drop — so a drop that can never sync again is reported as 'Synced' everywhere. This is the exact SWE-3/PBS-4 pattern the round-2 amendment claimed to close, re-created one layer up.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:368-373 `catch DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount { ... clearPending(drop.id); lastSyncError = ... }` — pending is dropped for a write that uploaded nothing (FirebaseDropStore.swift:55-57 throws before `setData` is ever reached). `lastSyncError` is a single global slot: DropStore.swift:365 sets it to nil on ANY other drop's successful ack, and DropStore.swift:237 sets it to nil whenever the cloud READ succeeds — and reads still succeed under a new uid (FirebaseDropStore.swift:32-34 just returns an empty set). With pending clear and lastSyncError nil, ProfileScreen.swift:88-95 falls through to 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops' and ShareDropSheet.swift:142-146 falls through to 'Sharing makes this drop visible to anyone with the link'. Nothing in the codebase ever rewrites a local drop's `ownerUid`, so the mismatch recurs on every launch forever.
findings.failureScenario: A user's drops acquire `ownerUid` locally: refresh() pulls ownerUid-bearing cloud copies into `drops` (DropStore.swift:229-235) and any later slider commit or share persists them to drops.json via update() -> local.save(). Their anonymous Firebase account is then reclaimed (Firebase's anonymous-account auto-cleanup after 30 days of inactivity, or a device restore without the keychain), so `signInAnonymously()` mints a NEW uid. On the next launch RootView.swift:121-124 fires refresh -> reconcileCloud -> performCloudSync for every pending drop; each throws `.ownedByAnotherAccount`, each has its pending flag cleared, and `lastSyncError` is set and then immediately nil'd by refresh's own successful (empty) cloud read at DropStore.swift:237. Profile now reads 'Synced — the server has confirmed your drops'. The user keeps creating and sharing for weeks; every share sheet says the link works. Nothing is in the cloud. On reinstall the entire library is gone, and every magic link they sent is dead.
findings.proposedFix: Do not clear pending on a terminal error. Add a `@Published private(set) var terminalSyncFailureIDs: Set<UUID>` (persisted alongside pendingSyncIDs), move the id there instead of calling clearPending, and have ProfileScreen/ShareDropSheet/DropsListScreen branch on it before the happy path. Separately, make `lastSyncError` non-clobbering: only the drop that owns the error may clear it (key errors by drop id), and never clear a write error from the read path at DropStore.swift:237. The ideal recovery is to adopt the drop — on `.ownedByAnotherAccount`, rewrite the local copy with `ownerUid = nil` via local.save and re-enqueue once — but visibility is the non-negotiable part.

testCase.name: testTerminalOwnerMismatchStaysVisibleAfterAnotherDropSyncs
testCase.steps: Arrange: extend StubCloudStore with `var failFor: [UUID: Error]` and a `loadResult: [GeoDrop]`. Build a DropLibrary over a temp LocalDropStore with that stub. Create drops A and B; set `cloud.failFor[A.id] = DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount`. Act: `try await library.add(A)`; `try await library.add(B)`; waitUntil { cloud.saveAttempts >= 2 }; then `await library.refresh(near: nil)` (stub read returns []). Assert: (1) the failure for A is still discoverable from the library's published state after B succeeded AND after the refresh — `XCTAssertTrue(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(A.id) || library.terminalSyncFailureIDs.contains(A.id))`; (2) `XCTAssertFalse(library.pendingSyncIDs.isEmpty && library.lastSyncError == nil, "a drop that can never sync must never present as fully synced")`; (3) `XCTAssertFalse(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(B.id))` — B's success must not be tainted either.
testCase.infrastructure: Extended StubCloudStore (per-id failure map + settable loadDrops result) in DropStoreTests.swift; temp-file LocalDropStore; setUp/tearDown must clear BOTH "pendingSyncDropIDs" and "pendingDeleteDropIDs" from UserDefaults.standard (DropStoreTests.swift:135-143 currently clears only the first). No emulator needed.

findings.claim: The whole-file quarantine warning erases itself on the very next load. `loadDrops` sets `pendingReadWarning = nil` when the file is absent — and the quarantine branch has just moved the file away — so the second load after a total library loss reports 'clean'. The launch sequence guarantees a second load within about a second, so the C7 guarantee ('an emptied library must never be silent') does not hold in the running app.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:108-114 moves drops.json to `.corrupt-<ts>` and sets the warning; DropStore.swift:84-87 `guard FileManager.default.fileExists(...) else { pendingReadWarning = nil; return [] }` — the next load finds no file and nils it. refresh() reads the verdict at DropStore.swift:224, so the banner (DropsListScreen.swift:49-53) is driven entirely by that nil-able value. AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 runs `refresh` at launch; RootView.swift:121-124 runs a second `refresh` the moment anonymous sign-in resolves (sub-second); MapScreen.swift:105-107 runs a third on tab appear. The same self-erasure exists for the partial-decode path: the first `save()` after a bad-row load rewrites drops.json without the bad rows (DropStore.swift:139-142), so the next load is 'clean' and the warning clears even though the rows were discarded — DropStoreTests.swift:102-106 asserts that as correct behaviour. The C7 test (DropStoreTests.swift:59-61) checks the warning after exactly ONE load and structurally cannot catch this.
findings.failureScenario: A user's drops.json is truncated by an unclean termination during `persist` (or hand-edited by a migration). Cold launch: AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 refresh #1 quarantines the file and sets 'Your saved drops couldn't be read — the file was kept on disk'; the user is on the Home tab and never sees the Sent tab. ~400 ms later anonymous auth resolves and RootView.swift:121-124 fires refresh #2; the file no longer exists, `pendingReadWarning` goes nil, `localReadWarning` goes nil. The user opens Sent and sees a cheerful 'No drops yet'. Their entire library was destroyed and the app told them nothing — the precise failure the amendment was written to prevent.
findings.proposedFix: Make the warning sticky until it is explicitly resolved rather than recomputed from the last load. Keep a persisted `lastDestructiveReadEvent` (UserDefaults or a marker file next to the quarantine) written in the quarantine branch and in the bad-row branch, and have the library publish it until the user dismisses it or a load returns a non-empty, fully-clean library. At minimum, do not nil the warning in the file-absent branch (DropStore.swift:85) — 'the file vanished' is not evidence of health.

testCase.name: testWholeFileQuarantineWarningSurvivesSubsequentLoads
testCase.steps: Arrange: temporaryFile(); write Data("this is not json {{{".utf8) to it; store = LocalDropStore(fileURL: url). Act: `_ = try await store.loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0)` (quarantines, file now gone); `_ = try await store.loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0)` (second load, file absent). Assert: `let warning = await store.lastLoadReadWarning(); XCTAssertNotNil(warning, "a destroyed library must stay reported across loads")`. Library-level companion in DropLibraryTests: seed the library's backing file with the same garbage, `await library.refresh(near: nil)` twice in a row, then `XCTAssertNotNil(library.localReadWarning)`.
testCase.infrastructure: Pure XCTest, temp file, existing LocalDropStore/DropLibrary test helpers (DropStoreTests.swift:6-16, :145-149). No device or emulator step.

findings.claim: When the local read throws, refresh() swallows it with `try?`, reports no failure at all, and then lets the stale cloud copy win the merge — after which `reconcileCloud()` re-uploads that stale copy and the server's ack clears the pending flag. The pipeline's central invariant ('only the server's accept of the LATEST write clears pending') is violated and the newer local edit is silently lost from the sync pipeline forever.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:88 `let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)` sits OUTSIDE the do/catch, so an I/O failure rethrows before `pendingReadWarning` is ever assigned — `lastLoadReadWarning()` keeps its previous (nil) value, which refresh then publishes at DropStore.swift:224. DropStore.swift:219 `if let localDrops = try? await local.loadDrops(...)` discards the error, and refresh never touches `lastPersistError`. With no local rows in `merged`, the anti-rollback guard at DropStore.swift:233 (`pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id), merged[drop.id] != nil`) fails on its second condition, so DropStore.swift:235 writes the stale server copy into `merged` and :244 publishes it. `reconcileCloud()` at :245 then reads the pending id out of `drops` — which now holds the STALE content (DropStore.swift:320) — and enqueues it; performCloudSync gets a real ack and calls `clearPending` at :364. There is no timestamp or version comparison anywhere in the merge.
findings.failureScenario: A user edits a previously-synced drop (moves it 4 m and rescales it) while offline. update() persists it locally and marks it pending; the Firestore continuation suspends because completions are not invoked offline. Connectivity returns. A refresh runs while the local read fails — a transient I/O error, an iCloud-restore placeholder, or a disk-pressure read failure on the Application Support container. refresh publishes no banner (localReadWarning nil, lastPersistError untouched, lastSyncError nil'd by the successful cloud read at :237), adopts the server's pre-edit copy, and reconcileCloud immediately pushes that pre-edit copy back to Firestore. The server acks, pending clears. The user's edit is still on disk but is now outside the pipeline: because pending is clear, every subsequent refresh overwrites it in memory with the server copy (:235). The drop snaps back to its old position and size on every launch, permanently, with no error shown at any point.
findings.proposedFix: Three changes. (1) Set `pendingReadWarning` before rethrowing in loadDrops — move the `Data(contentsOf:)` call inside a do/catch that records 'Your saved drops couldn't be read' and rethrows. (2) In refresh, replace `try?` at :219 with a do/catch that sets `lastPersistError` (or a dedicated `localReadError`) and — critically — SKIPS the cloud merge and the `drops =` publish entirely when the local read failed, since a merge without local truth cannot be correct. (3) Have reconcileCloud re-read the pending drop from `local` rather than from the post-merge `drops` array, so it can never push a copy the cloud read just installed.

testCase.name: testFailingLocalReadNeitherHidesTheFailureNorClearsPending
testCase.steps: Arrange: a `ThrowingLocalStore: DropStore` stub with `var throwOnLoad = false`, a real in-memory dictionary for save/delete, and `loadDrops` that throws NSError(domain:"io", code:5) when the flag is set. A StubCloudStore whose `loadDrops` returns [staleCopy] (same id, `message == "old"`) and whose `save` records full payloads. Act: `cloud.failWith = DropStoreError.notSignedIn`; `try await library.update(newCopy)` where newCopy.message == "new"; waitUntil { library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(id) }; `cloud.failWith = nil`; `local.throwOnLoad = true`; `await library.refresh(near: nil)`; waitUntil-or-settle 200 ms. Assert: (1) `XCTAssertTrue(library.lastPersistError != nil || library.localReadWarning != nil, "a failed local read must be visible")`; (2) `XCTAssertFalse(cloud.savedPayloads.contains { $0.message == "old" }, "reconcile must never push a copy the cloud read just installed")`; (3) `XCTAssertTrue(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(id), "pending may only clear on an ack of the latest write")`.
testCase.infrastructure: New ThrowingLocalStore stub and a StubCloudStore extended to record full GeoDrop payloads (not just ids) and to return a settable loadDrops result. Both @MainActor, in DropStoreTests.swift. No emulator; no device step.

findings.claim: refresh() publishes `drops` from a `merged` snapshot computed before its two awaits, so any add/update/remove that lands during the awaits is clobbered. For a delete this resurrects a drop that is already gone from disk and tombstoned, and the resurrected row is fully interactive — re-sharing or re-adjusting it writes it back to disk and re-uploads it while its tombstone is still live, leaving local and cloud permanently inconsistent.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:217-244: `merged` is populated from `local.loadDrops` (await) and `cloud.loadDrops` (await), then :244 assigns `drops = merged.values.sorted { ... }` — an unconditional whole-array replacement with no epoch/generation check, even though `remove()` (:297) and `add()` (:260-261) mutate `drops` from the same actor during those awaits. The tombstone guard at :234 filters only the CLOUD list; the local snapshot taken before the delete is never re-filtered against `pendingDeleteIDs`. reconcileCloud at :245 then runs against the clobbered array: at :320 `drops.first(where:)` returns the resurrected drop for a delete, or nil for a concurrent add (skipping its push). MapScreen.swift puts both triggers on one screen — `.task(id:)` refresh at :105-107 and the destructive context-menu `Task { try? await library.remove(drop) }` at :36 — and DropsListScreen has the refresh button at :26 next to `.onDelete` at :92-98.
findings.failureScenario: On the Explore tab the user long-presses a drop and taps 'Remove drop' just as the `.task(id: locationService.location == nil)` refresh re-fires on the first GPS fix. refresh is suspended in `cloud.loadDrops`; remove() completes — local.delete succeeds, the drop leaves `drops`, pendingSync is cleared, a tombstone is written to UserDefaults and the cloud delete is launched. refresh then resumes and assigns `drops` from its pre-delete snapshot: the deleted drop is back on the map and in the Sent list. The user assumes the delete failed and taps 'Send the magic link' on the ghost row; ShareDropSheet.sendLink() calls `library.update(sharedDrop)`, which writes the drop back to drops.json and marks it pending, and enqueueCloudSync re-uploads it. Its id is still in `pendingDeleteIDs`, so refresh() at :234 now permanently filters the cloud copy out of every future merge while the local copy persists — the drop the user deleted is alive on disk and in Firestore, and the two can never reconcile.
findings.proposedFix: Version the publish. Add `private var refreshGeneration: UInt64`; bump it at the top of refresh and in every mutator (add/update/remove); before line 244, bail out or re-merge if the generation changed during the awaits. Cheaper and equally correct: build `merged` starting from the CURRENT `drops` array rather than replacing it, and apply `pendingDeleteIDs` as a filter over the whole merged set (not just the cloud list) immediately before publishing, so a tombstoned id can never be published from any source.

testCase.name: testDeleteDuringRefreshIsNotResurrectedByThePublish
testCase.steps: Arrange: a StubCloudStore whose `loadDrops` awaits a test-owned CheckedContinuation before returning [] (a `gate`), and which records delete attempts. Library over a temp LocalDropStore with that cloud. `try await library.add(drop)`; waitUntil { !library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id) }. Act: `let refreshTask = Task { await library.refresh(near: nil) }`; waitUntil { cloud.loadDropsEntered }; `try await library.remove(drop)`; resume the gate; `await refreshTask.value`. Assert: (1) `XCTAssertFalse(library.drops.contains { $0.id == drop.id }, "a delete that completed must not be resurrected by an in-flight refresh")`; (2) `let onDisk = try await localStore.loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0); XCTAssertTrue(onDisk.isEmpty)`; (3) run `await library.refresh(near: nil)` a second time and assert `library.drops.isEmpty`. Add a sibling `testAddDuringRefreshSurvivesThePublish` asserting `library.drops.contains { $0.id == newDrop.id }` and `library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(newDrop.id)`.
testCase.infrastructure: StubCloudStore extended with a test-controlled continuation gate on loadDrops and a `deleteAttempts` counter (the current stub's delete is a bare no-op, DropStoreTests.swift:252). Temp-file LocalDropStore. setUp/tearDown must clear both pending UserDefaults keys. No emulator, no device step.

findings.claim: Batch delete runs `try? await library.remove(drop)` in a sequential loop, and each successful remove sets `lastPersistError = nil` — so a delete that fails inside a multi-row batch has its banner erased by the very next success, and the surviving row silently reappears in the list with no explanation. The comment on line 95 ('Failures surface via lastPersistError banner') is false whenever the failing drop is not the last one.
findings.evidence: DropsListScreen.swift:92-98 `let doomed = indexSet.map { library.drops[$0] }` then `for drop in doomed { try? await library.remove(drop) }`. DropStore.swift:293 sets `lastPersistError` on failure, but DropStore.swift:296 sets `lastPersistError = nil` on the next success — a single global slot with last-writer-wins. Because remove() throws before mutating `drops` (:297), the failed row is still in `library.drops`, so SwiftUI re-renders it back into the List after having animated it out. The same clobber applies across mutation kinds: an `add` or `update` succeeding right after a failed `remove` (DropStore.swift:259, :282) also nils the banner. MapScreen.swift:36 uses the identical `try?` shape for its single-row delete.
findings.failureScenario: The user enters edit mode on the Sent tab, selects three drops and deletes them. The container is momentarily unwritable (disk pressure / a data-protection window right after a lock). Drop 1's `local.delete` throws — `lastPersistError` is set and the throw is swallowed by `try?`. Drops 2 and 3 delete successfully and each resets `lastPersistError` to nil. The list settles showing drop 1 still present, no banner, no alert. The user believes the app randomly refused one deletion; the next time they delete it, the drop may go — or may not — with the same silence. For a user deleting content they want gone (a drop with someone's name on it), an undetectable failure to delete is a trust failure, not a cosmetic one.
findings.proposedFix: Make failure reporting additive rather than last-writer-wins: replace `lastPersistError: String?` with a small `[UUID: String]` (or an ordered array of failure records) that only the owning drop's next SUCCESS may clear, and have `banners` (DropsListScreen.swift:37-62) render the set. Then change the loop at :92-98 to collect the thrown errors and present the aggregate ('2 of 3 drops couldn't be deleted') rather than discarding them with `try?`.

testCase.name: testFailedDeleteInABatchStaysReportedAfterLaterSuccesses
testCase.steps: Arrange: a `FlakyLocalStore: DropStore` backed by an in-memory dictionary whose `delete` throws NSError(domain:"disk", code:28) for a designated `poisonID` and succeeds otherwise. Library over it with `cloudStore: nil`. `try await library.add(A)`, `try await library.add(B)`, `try await library.add(C)`; set `local.poisonID = A.id`. Act: mirror the screen's loop exactly — `for drop in [A, B, C] { try? await library.remove(drop) }`. Assert: (1) `XCTAssertNotNil(library.lastPersistError, "a failed delete must stay reported after later successes")`; (2) `XCTAssertTrue(library.lastPersistError?.contains("delete") == true)`; (3) `XCTAssertEqual(library.drops.map(\.id), [A.id])` — the failed drop is still present, so the banner is the only signal the user has.
testCase.infrastructure: New FlakyLocalStore stub (@MainActor or actor, conforming to DropStore) in DropStoreTests.swift. No emulator. A device field step is worth pairing with it: trigger a real write failure by filling the container, batch-delete three drops on the Sent tab, and confirm the banner is visible after the batch settles.

additionalTests.name: testSupersededSyncTaskCannotClearPendingWhenItFinallyResumes
additionalTests.pins: The C2/C22 generation guard in performCloudSync (DropStore.swift:341-342, :356, :363, :371, :375) — the entire reason the round-2 amendment exists. Nothing in the current 59-test suite creates two overlapping writes for one drop, so the guard is completely unexercised: deleting every `syncGenerations` check would leave the suite green.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: StubCloudStore whose `save` parks on a test-owned CheckedContinuation keyed by the payload's `message`, and which records the full ordered payload list. Library over a temp LocalDropStore. Act: `try await library.update(v1)` (message "v1") and wait until the stub reports it entered save for v1 (it stays parked — the offline continuation). `try await library.update(v2)` (message "v2"); release v2's continuation successfully; waitUntil { !library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(id) }. Now release v1's continuation successfully — the superseded task resumes at last. Assert: (1) `XCTAssertFalse(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(id), "a superseded task must not re-open or re-clear bookkeeping it no longer owns")`; (2) `XCTAssertEqual(cloud.savedPayloads.last?.message, "v2")`; (3) `XCTAssertNil(library.lastSyncError)`. Then a negative variant: release v1 with a thrown NSError instead and assert `library.lastSyncError == nil` — a stale generation must not raise a banner for a write nobody is waiting on.
additionalTests.infrastructure: StubCloudStore extended with per-payload CheckedContinuation parking (a `[String: CheckedContinuation<Void, Error>]` plus an `entered: Set<String>`) and full payload recording. All @MainActor, in DropStoreTests.swift. No emulator, no device step.

additionalTests.name: testDeleteTombstoneSurvivesRelaunchAndIsReplayedOnAuthReady
additionalTests.pins: The C3 durable delete tombstone (DropStore.swift:305-306, :324-326, :380-401, :419-433) and refresh's don't-resurrect rule (:234). The tombstone path has zero coverage today — DropLibraryTests' only remove() call runs with `cloudStore: nil` (DropStoreTests.swift:169), which returns at the `guard cloud != nil` on :304 before a tombstone is ever written, and setUp/tearDown (DropStoreTests.swift:135-143) never even clears the "pendingDeleteDropIDs" key.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: StubCloudStore with a `deleted: [UUID]` recorder and a settable `deleteFailure`; set `deleteFailure = DropStoreError.notSignedIn`; give the stub a `loadResult` containing the drop (the server still has it). Library #1 over a fixed temp file URL. `try await library1.add(drop)`; wait for the ack. Act: `try await library1.remove(drop)`; waitUntil { cloud.deleteAttempts > 0 }. Assert phase 1: `XCTAssertEqual(UserDefaults.standard.stringArray(forKey: "pendingDeleteDropIDs"), [drop.id.uuidString])`; `await library1.refresh(near: nil)`; `XCTAssertFalse(library1.drops.contains { $0.id == drop.id }, "a live tombstone must not let the cloud read resurrect the drop")`. Act phase 2 (simulated relaunch): construct library2 over the SAME file URL and the same cloud stub with `deleteFailure = nil`; `library2.reconcileCloud()`; waitUntil { cloud.deleted.contains(drop.id) }. Assert: `XCTAssertEqual(UserDefaults.standard.stringArray(forKey: "pendingDeleteDropIDs") ?? [], [])`.
additionalTests.infrastructure: StubCloudStore extended with delete recording, a settable delete failure and a settable loadDrops result. Fixed (not per-call random) temp file URL so library2 sees library1's disk state. setUp/tearDown MUST clear both "pendingSyncDropIDs" and "pendingDeleteDropIDs" — add the second key to DropStoreTests.swift:135-143 before writing this test, or it will pollute later tests and the host app's defaults. No emulator.

additionalTests.name: testAckedFirestoreWriteReportsRulesRejectionAndKeepsDropPending
additionalTests.pins: The PBS-4 acked-write continuation itself (FirebaseDropStore.swift:76-90) and the AccountService twin (AccountService.swift:99-116). The whole point of the change is that a rules rejection now propagates instead of resolving on local staging — and no test in the suite ever runs the real FirebaseDropStore. FirebaseIntegrationTests.swift is 675 bytes and does not touch the write path.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: Firestore emulator running with a deny-all rules file for the `drops` collection; app configured against the emulator host; sign in anonymously against the Auth emulator. Act: `let store = FirebaseDropStore(); do { try await store.save(GeoDrop()) ; XCTFail("a denied write must throw") } catch { XCTAssertEqual((error as NSError).domain, FirestoreErrorDomain) }`. Then wire it end-to-end: `let library = DropLibrary(localStore: LocalDropStore(fileURL: temp), cloudStore: store)`; `try await library.add(drop)`; waitUntil { library.lastSyncError != nil }. Assert: `XCTAssertTrue(library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id), "a rules-rejected write must stay pending")` and `XCTAssertFalse(library.lastSyncError?.isEmpty ?? true)`. Second case with permissive rules: assert the same call succeeds and `pendingSyncIDs` empties. Third case, offline: put the emulator behind a disabled network (or call `Firestore.firestore().disableNetwork()`), assert the save neither returns nor throws within 1 s and the drop stays pending — the documented offline-completion behaviour the pipeline depends on.
additionalTests.infrastructure: Firestore + Auth emulators (firebase emulators:start) with two rules fixtures (deny-all and permissive), an emulator-pointing FirebaseApp configuration in the test target, and `Firestore.firestore().disableNetwork()` for the offline case. This is the one test in the set that cannot run as a pure unit test; it belongs in an integration scheme, not the 59-test device suite.

soundAreas: LocalDropStore actor reentrancy (DropStore.swift:83-149): loadDrops contains no suspension point at all — Data(contentsOf:), JSONDecoder, FileManager, preserveUnreadable and persist are all synchronous — so `try await loadDrops(...)` inside save/delete is a same-actor call that cannot interleave. The load-modify-write really is atomic per store instance, and testConcurrentSavesAllSurvive (DropStoreTests.swift:109) pins it. SWE-8 is genuinely closed.

C5 rethrow (DropStore.swift:139,146): save/delete now rethrow the read error, so the one path that could atomically erase the library (a file that reads but throws) can no longer persist [] over it; the missing-file (line 84) and post-quarantine (line 114) paths still legitimately return [] and both set pendingReadWarning first, so no emptying is silent.

Sidecar/quarantine hygiene (DropStore.swift:108-129): content-digest naming plus the fileExists short-circuit yields exactly one sidecar per DISTINCT corrupt payload across repeated loads and relaunches, and the whole-file quarantine is timestamped so a second failure cannot overwrite the first backup. C6/C14/C24 hold.

ARP-3 latch (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2095-2107): farMode is now computed unconditionally with geospatial.semanticActive as a term, so semanticMatteArmed can fall in the 15-55 m band and passNeeded (line 1037-1047) can reach the setCallbacksActive(false) branch. `&&` short-circuits, so the placedHolders scan still does not run when semantics are off, and SemanticFeed.setEnabled is one NSLock write (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:27-31) — negligible at 60 Hz. No new per-frame cost.

SWE-6 retry loop (DropEntityFactory.swift:137-140, 218-221): failedAssets.insert happens BEFORE onAssetLoaded?(name,false) on both decode paths (lines 118-123, 141-144), and the negative cache is consulted in requestAsset and animatedModel, so assetTemplateDidLoad's rebuild resolves to the "3D?" text and terminates. The loop is genuinely broken. (Note: preloadAnimatedAssets' filter at line 106 omits failedAssets, but ARSessionHolder.configure is idempotent (ARSessionHolder.swift:26-37) so preload runs once per process — latent trap, not a live defect.)

Generation bookkeeping completeness (DropStore.swift:298-301, 336-347): every mutation of syncTasks/pendingSyncIDs outside enqueueCloudSync goes through remove(), which bumps the generation first; enqueueCloudSync always installs the current-generation task, so syncTasks[id] never holds a stale registration and reconcileCloud's `syncTasks[id] == nil` gate cannot be permanently blocked by a superseded task. C2/C22 are correct as far as the post-write guards go (see finding 3 for the pre-write gap).

Main-actor inheritance (DropStore.swift:344,382; GeoARSessionManager.swift:90,1616,1789): all five new unstructured Tasks are created in @MainActor synchronous contexts and use the implicit @_inheritActorContext closure, so their bodies — including performCloudSync's `defer` that mutates syncTasks — run on the main actor. No isolated state is touched from a detached context, and `syncTasks[id] = Task {...}` cannot be clobbered by its own body because the assignment completes before the main actor yields.

remove() ordering (DropStore.swift:286-307): disk delete first, bookkeeping destroyed only on success, receivedViaLink filtered before markPendingDelete. A failed local delete leaves the drop visible, the pending flag alive, no tombstone, and both publishes and throws. C13/C26 hold.

Transient AR error timer (GeoARSessionManager.swift:87-95): cancel-then-replace is fully synchronous on the main actor, and `guard !Task.isCancelled` after `try? await Task.sleep` correctly stops a cancelled timer from clearing a newer message. No stuck or cross-clearing banner.

DropsListScreen banner restructure (DropsListScreen.swift:15-18, 36-61): banners sit above the empty/list split, so a fully unreadable library shows the warning alongside "No drops yet" rather than a silent cheerful empty state. C12 holds.

findings.claim: The terminal `ownedByAnotherAccount` outcome is recorded ONLY in the shared, non-durable `lastSyncError` string while the drop is simultaneously removed from `pendingSyncIDs`. Any later success — another drop's write or any successful cloud read — erases the string, after which the app reports "Synced" for a drop that will provably never reach the server. This re-creates SWE-3's exact failure inside the SWE-3/C4/C15 fix.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:368-373 `catch DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount { ... clearPending(drop.id); lastSyncError = ... }` — the only record of a permanent failure is one `@Published var lastSyncError: String?` (line 176). It is unconditionally nil'd by the success path at line 365 (`lastSyncError = nil` after any acknowledged write) and by the successful-read path at line 237 (`lastSyncError = nil` inside refresh, which every tab switch and launch triggers). Because `clearPending` also ran, `pendingSyncIDs` no longer contains the drop and `reconcileCloud` (line 319) will never retry it. ProfileScreen.swift:77-89 then falls through `else if let error = library.lastSyncError` and `else if !library.pendingSyncIDs.isEmpty` to `Label("Synced — the server has confirmed your drops")`. The throw site is FirebaseDropStore.swift:55-57 `if let owner = drop.ownerUid, owner != uid { throw DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount }`.
findings.failureScenario: The device reboots and the user launches the app before the first unlock completes, so the Firebase Auth keychain item is unreadable: `Auth.auth().currentUser` is nil (AccountService.swift:22) and `signInAnonymously()` mints a BRAND NEW uid. Every drop the user has previously refreshed-then-edited or shared carries the OLD `ownerUid` (refresh puts cloud copies with `ownerUid` into `drops` at DropStore.swift:235, and the next `update` persists them at line 277). RootView.swift:121-124 fires the auth-ready refresh; `reconcileCloud` pushes all 20 drops; all 20 throw `ownedByAnotherAccount`; all 20 are cleared from pending; `lastSyncError` shows one orange line for a moment. The user taps the Map tab — MapScreen's refresh runs, the cloud READ succeeds (it just returns zero docs for the new uid), line 237 sets `lastSyncError = nil`. Sent tab: no banner. Profile: "Synced — the server has confirmed your drops". The entire library is now cloud-orphaned, every previously shared magic link points at documents that will never be updated again, and nothing in the app will ever retry or ever say so.
findings.proposedFix: Add a durable per-drop terminal-failure set (`unsyncableIDs`, persisted next to `pendingSyncIDs` in UserDefaults) written in the `ownedByAnotherAccount` catch; render it per-row in DropsListScreen and as a distinct Profile state that ranks ABOVE "Synced". Make `lastSyncError` per-drop (`[UUID: String]`) so one drop's success cannot clear another's failure, and stop clearing it wholesale on a successful read at line 237.

findings.claim: `seedProfile` is re-entrant and never re-checks whether a profile has arrived. `profile` is assigned only AFTER the acked write returns, so the listener's `self.profile == nil` gate stays open for the entire seed (up to ~4.5 s with the two sleeps), letting further snapshot events start additional independent 3-attempt loops; and a late attempt writes the starter payload with `merge: true` over a profile that arrived in the meantime, both locally and on the server.
findings.evidence: AccountService.swift:58-64: the listener branch guards on `self.profile == nil` and then `await self.seedProfile(uid: uid)`. AccountService.swift:70-94: `for attempt in 1...3 { try await Self.setDataAcked(...); profile = starter; return } catch { ... try? await Task.sleep(nanoseconds: UInt64(attempt) * 1_500_000_000) }` — there is no in-flight flag, no re-check of `profile == nil` before the write or before `profile = starter`, and no abort. `setDataAcked` (line 99-116) now suspends until the SERVER answers, which widens the window from microseconds (the old fire-and-forget `setData`) to a full round trip plus up to 4.5 s of backoff. `includeMetadataChanges: true` (line 46) strictly increases the number of delivered events, and a rules-rejected write causes Firestore to roll back the local mutation, producing another server-sourced `!exists` event that re-satisfies the gate. `updateProfile` (line 120-141) writes concurrently with `merge: true` on the same document.
findings.failureScenario: First launch on a flaky connection. The server-confirmed absence event fires and seed attempt 1 fails with `unavailable`; the loop sleeps 1.5 s. Within that window the user is already on the You tab, types "Adnan" / "adnan" and taps save: `updateProfile` sets `profile` and fires its own acked write, which succeeds. At t≈1.5 s the seed's attempt 2 runs — it never re-checks `profile` — and writes `handle: "guest-abc123"`, `displayName: "New Dropper"` with `merge: true`, then sets `profile = starter`. The user's name and handle are silently reverted on the device AND on the server, with no error shown, and every subsequent snapshot confirms the reverted values. This is the PBS-7 outcome the wave was written to eliminate, reached through the new retry loop. The fan-out variant: with rules denying `users/{uid}` writes, each failed attempt produces a rollback event that starts another 3-attempt loop, which produces more failures — concurrent seed loops grow without bound for as long as the app is foregrounded.
findings.proposedFix: Make the seed single-flight: store `private var seedTask: Task<Void, Never>?`, set it synchronously in the listener before any await, and `guard seedTask == nil` there. Inside the loop, re-check `guard profile == nil else { return }` immediately before each `setDataAcked` call and again immediately before `profile = starter`. Cancel/short-circuit the loop from the `snapshot.exists` branch (line 49-57) and from `updateProfile` the moment a real profile exists.

testCase.name: testSeedIsSingleFlightAndNeverOverwritesAnArrivedProfile
testCase.steps: Arrange: extract the two Firestore seams — replace `Self.setDataAcked` with an injectable `var writeProfile: (String, UserProfile) async throws -> Void` and expose the listener decision as `func handleProfileSnapshot(exists: Bool, fromCache: Bool, decoded: UserProfile?) async`. Configure `writeProfile` to throw NSError(domain: "FIRFirestoreErrorDomain", code: 14 /*unavailable*/) on its first invocation and succeed thereafter, recording every (uid, payload) it receives. Assert: (1) the starter payload was offered to `writeProfile` at most once per attempt of a SINGLE loop (i.e. no more than 3 total invocations with `displayName == "New Dropper"`), proving single-flight; (2) `service.profile?.handle == "adnan"` and `service.profile?.displayName == "Adnan"` at the end; (3) no `writeProfile` invocation carrying the starter payload occurred at a point where `service.profile != nil`. Today (1) records 6 invocations and (2) reads back "guest-..."/"New Dropper".

findings.claim: `performCloudSync` checks the generation only AFTER `cloud.save` returns; there is no entry-time generation or cancellation check. Combined with the fact that `syncTasks[id]?.cancel()` cannot interrupt the checked continuation wrapping Firestore's completion handler, a superseded task still issues a full write of stale data, and superseded tasks accumulate for the whole offline period instead of being shed.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:349-362: `private func performCloudSync(...) async { guard let cloud else { return }; defer {...}; do { try await cloud.save(drop) ... }` — the first guard on `syncGenerations[drop.id] == generation` appears at line 363, after the write. A Task cancelled before its body starts still runs its body (cooperative cancellation), so `syncTasks[drop.id]?.cancel()` at line 343 provides zero back-pressure. FirebaseDropStore.swift:76-90 wraps `document.setData(from:merge:) { error in ... }` in `withCheckedThrowingContinuation` with no `withTaskCancellationHandler`, and per researcher Theme 12 (COUNSEL-RAW-OUTPUT:1119-1139, Firebase iOS SDK issues #2167/#3303) that completion is not invoked at all while offline — so a cancelled task parks indefinitely holding a continuation and a GeoDrop copy.
findings.failureScenario: A 40-minute field session in a dead zone. Every slider release commits (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1616) and every "Place on ground"/"Pin to a spot" commits (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1789), each calling `update(persist: true)` -> `enqueueCloudSync`. After 40 adjustments to one drop there are 40 live Tasks, 40 checked continuations, and 40 queued Firestore mutations against the same document `drops/{id}`. On reconnect all 40 flush at once against Firestore's ~1 sustained write/sec per-document limit; 39 of them write payloads the user has already superseded. If the 40th (current-generation) write is the one that comes back `aborted`/contention, it lands in the generic catch at line 374-377, the drop stays in `pendingSyncIDs`, and ProfileScreen shows "Uploading 1 drop…" indefinitely while 39 stale copies were billed and written.
findings.proposedFix: Make `guard !Task.isCancelled, syncGenerations[drop.id] == generation else { return }` the first statement of `performCloudSync` (before `guard let cloud`), so a generation superseded before its body ran issues no write at all. Additionally wrap the Firestore continuation in `withTaskCancellationHandler` so a cancelled write resumes promptly rather than parking, and consider coalescing: if `syncTasks[id] != nil`, record that a re-push is needed instead of stacking a second in-flight write.

findings.claim: `refresh()` is not serialized and ends by replacing `drops` wholesale from a snapshot captured before its awaits. The change set adds a SECOND refresh trigger that fires exactly when anonymous auth resolves — a second or two into launch, squarely inside the create flow — so the losing refresh republishes a pre-save snapshot and a just-created drop disappears from the UI.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:217-246: `refresh` builds a local `merged` dictionary, awaits `local.loadDrops` and then `cloud.loadDrops`, and finally assigns `drops = merged.values.sorted { ... }` (line 244) — an unconditional wholesale replace with no guard that a newer refresh has since run or that `drops` was mutated during the awaits. There is no `isRefreshing`/generation token anywhere in the class. RootView.swift:121-124 adds `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-") { await library.refresh(near: nil) }`, which fires the moment `signInAnonymously()` returns, while AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:34 already runs `await dropLibrary.refresh(near: locationService.location)` at launch. `add` mutates `drops` at lines 260-262 with no interlock.
findings.failureScenario: Cold launch with Firebase configured. The app-level refresh runs pre-auth; its cloud read throws `.notSignedIn` and is swallowed at line 238. ~1-2 s later anonymous sign-in resolves, `account.uid` flips, and RootView's new `.task(id:)` starts a second refresh whose `getDocuments()` takes a few hundred ms. In that window the user finishes the Create wizard: `add()` writes to disk and inserts the drop into `drops`, and CreateWizard.swift:642-643 opens ShareDropSheet for it. The in-flight refresh then resumes and executes `drops = merged.values.sorted { ... }` from a `merged` built BEFORE the disk write — the new drop vanishes from the Sent list and the Map, `ReactionService.listenKey(for: library.drops, ...)` (RootView.swift:114) re-fires without it so the sender stops listening for reactions to the drop they are at that moment sharing, and the open ShareDropSheet's `library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id)` banner state no longer corresponds to anything in `library.drops`. It only reappears on the next refresh.
findings.proposedFix: Add a monotonic `refreshGeneration: UInt64`; capture it at the top of `refresh`, and at line 244 `guard refreshGeneration == captured else { return }` before assigning `drops` (and before `lastSyncError`/`localReadWarning`). Better still, merge the refresh result into the existing `drops` keyed by id instead of replacing the array, so a drop added during the awaits is never dropped.

findings.claim: The new DropLibraryTests mutate the SHIPPING app's `UserDefaults.standard` keys directly and never reset the newly introduced `pendingDeleteDropIDs`. Running the suite on a real device destroys that device's pending upload outbox and silently discards its delete tombstones, and leaves the delete key dirty across test cases.
findings.evidence: DropStoreTests.swift:135-143: `override func setUp() { UserDefaults.standard.removeObject(forKey: "pendingSyncDropIDs") }` and the identical `tearDown` — the same literal key the app writes at DropStore.swift:414-416. `pendingDeleteDropIDs` (DropStore.swift:198, 429-432) is never cleared in either hook. `makeLibrary` (DropStoreTests.swift:145-149) constructs a real DropLibrary, whose init reads both keys from `UserDefaults.standard` (DropStore.swift:211-214). `reconcileCloud`, which `testPendingSyncClearsOnlyOnAcknowledgedWrite` calls explicitly, then replays every id in `pendingDeleteIDs` through `launchCloudDelete` (line 324-326).
findings.failureScenario: A developer runs the verified 59-test device suite on their own iPhone, which has the app installed with three drops queued for upload and two tombstones awaiting replay. `setUp` removes `pendingSyncDropIDs`: because `reconcileCloud` only ever pushes ids present in `pendingSyncIDs` (line 319, the deliberate C1/C10/C21 behaviour), those three drops are now unreachable by any retry path and are never uploaded — the exact outbox-wipe the round-2 fix was written to prevent, reintroduced by the test harness. Meanwhile `makeLibrary(cloud: StubCloudStore())` loads the two real tombstones, `library.reconcileCloud()` hands them to the stub whose `delete` is an empty no-op (DropStoreTests.swift:2036), the catch-free success path calls `clearPendingDelete`, and the two Firestore documents are orphaned in the cloud forever. The same leakage makes the sync tests order- and device-dependent.
findings.proposedFix: Add a `defaults: UserDefaults = .standard` parameter to `DropLibrary.init` and route `persistPending`/`persistPendingDeletes`/init reads through it; have `makeLibrary` pass `UserDefaults(suiteName: "DropLibraryTests-\(UUID().uuidString)")` and remove the `UserDefaults.standard` mutations from setUp/tearDown entirely. As a stopgap, at minimum also clear `pendingDeleteDropIDs` in both hooks.

findings.claim: The `DropStore` seam now has three implementations on three different isolations — `LocalDropStore` is an actor, `FirebaseDropStore` is a nonisolated final class, `StubCloudStore` is @MainActor — behind a protocol that is not Sendable. The immediate consequence is that the test double never suspends where production always does, so the new generation guards are structurally unexercised; the downstream consequence is that this seam blocks the Swift 6 migration.
findings.evidence: DropStore.swift:8-13 declares `protocol DropStore` with no Sendable conformance; DropStore.swift:186-187 stores it as `private let local: DropStore` / `cloud: DropStore?` inside a @MainActor class. LocalDropStore is `actor` (line 40), FirebaseDropStore is `final class` with no isolation (FirebaseDropStore.swift:15), and the round-2 C25 fix made StubCloudStore `@MainActor` (DropStoreTests.swift:2020-2021). Per SE-0338, `try await cloud.save(drop)` at DropStore.swift:362 hops OFF the main actor for FirebaseDropStore but does not hop at all for the @MainActor stub, whose `save` (DropStoreTests.swift:2030-2034) contains no await and therefore never suspends. project.pbxproj:363 shows `SWIFT_VERSION = 5.0` with no `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY` setting, so the non-Sendable existential crossing is not diagnosed today.
findings.failureScenario: Concrete today: because `StubCloudStore.save` never suspends, `performCloudSync` runs to completion inside a single main-actor turn in every test, so no other main-actor work (a second `enqueueCloudSync`, a `remove`, a `refresh`) can ever interleave with it. `testPendingSyncClearsOnlyOnAcknowledgedWrite` and `testCloudFailureIsVisibleAndStaysPending` therefore pin zero of the C2/C22 generation behaviour they were added for — which is precisely why finding 3's missing entry guard survives a green 59-test run. Concrete tomorrow: switching the target to `SWIFT_STRICT_CONCURRENCY = complete` / `SWIFT_VERSION = 6.0` makes `try await cloud.save(drop)` from `@MainActor DropLibrary` on a non-Sendable `any DropStore` a hard compile error, along with the nonisolated default argument `cloudStore: DropStore? = ... FirebaseDropStore() ...` at DropStore.swift:205-207 — the migration is blocked at the seam this wave just rebuilt.
findings.proposedFix: Declare `protocol DropStore: Sendable`, mark `FirebaseDropStore` as `final class ... : DropStore` with stateless `Sendable` conformance (it holds no stored properties), and make the test double nonisolated with an internal lock or an actor rather than @MainActor — so every implementation suspends at the same points production does. Then add a warning-only CI lane building with `-strict-concurrency=complete` to keep the seam Swift 6 ready.

additionalTests.name: testCacheOnlyAbsenceNeverSeedsAndServerAbsenceSeedsExactlyOnce
additionalTests.pins: The PBS-7 gate `!snapshot.metadata.isFromCache` and the C11 `includeMetadataChanges: true` change (AccountService.swift:46, 58-60) and the C23 decode-failure branch (49-57). Nothing in AugmentMeRealityTests touches AccountService at all — the entire profile lifecycle, including the reinstall case that motivated PBS-7, is currently unpinned.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: the `handleProfileSnapshot(exists:fromCache:decoded:)` seam from finding 2's test plus a recording `writeProfile` closure. Act/Assert in sequence: (1) `handleProfileSnapshot(exists: false, fromCache: true, decoded: nil)` -> `writeProfile` never invoked (a cache miss is "don't know yet", not "first run"); (2) `handleProfileSnapshot(exists: false, fromCache: false, decoded: nil)` -> invoked exactly once with the starter payload; (3) `handleProfileSnapshot(exists: true, fromCache: false, decoded: nil /* decode throws */)` -> `writeProfile` invocation count unchanged and `service.profile` unchanged, proving a schema-drifted but EXISTING doc is never seeded over; (4) `handleProfileSnapshot(exists: true, fromCache: false, decoded: realProfile)` followed by another `(exists: false, fromCache: false, decoded: nil)` -> still no further write, proving a stale absence event after a real profile arrived cannot re-seed. additionalTests.name: testFailedAssetShowsTheMarkerOnceAndIsNeverRedecoded
additionalTests.pins: The SWE-6 negative cache and the C19/C20 in-AR surfacing: `failedAssets` gating `requestAsset` (DropEntityFactory.swift:137-140) and `animatedModel` (218-221), the `(String, Bool)` callback contract (line 66), and `GeoARSessionManager.showPersistError` firing on the failure branch (line 321-325). The suite's only asset test is AssetLoadStallTests (main-thread stall timing) — nothing pins the failure path, and the `preloadAnimatedAssets` filter at line 106 omits `failedAssets`, which this test would expose the moment preload ever becomes re-entrant.
additionalTests.steps: Arrange: on-device (RealityKit decode requires real hardware), add a deliberately corrupt `broken.usdz` fixture to the test bundle and a decode-count spy (either an injectable `decodeTemplate` seam or a counter incremented in the existing decode path). Act: build a GeoDrop with `content == .animated, assetName == "broken"` and call `DropEntityFactory.makeEntity(for:fullBright:)`; wait for the decode to fail; call `makeEntity` five more times for the same drop; also invoke `DropEntityFactory.preloadAnimatedAssets()` a second time. Assert: (1) the spy records exactly one decode attempt across all six builds and the second preload — no retry loop, and the preload filter respects the negative cache; (2) the entity returned after the failure is the "3D?" text marker, not `loadingPlaceholder` (check the entity's ModelComponent mesh kind or a test-only tag); (3) `onAssetLoaded` was invoked exactly once with `success == false`; (4) driving that callback through GeoARSessionManager sets `manager.persistErrorText` and it auto-clears after >4 s (GeoARSessionManager.swift:90-94).
additionalTests.infrastructure: On-device XCTest run (iPhone 15 Pro Max, matching the existing device suite); a corrupt `broken.usdz` fixture in the test bundle; a decode-count spy seam on DropEntityFactory. The 4-second auto-clear assertion needs either an injectable clock or an XCTestExpectation with a >5 s timeout.

soundAreas: SWE-6 retry loop is genuinely closed: failedAssets is inserted BEFORE onAssetLoaded fires (DropEntityFactory.swift:120-123, 141-144), gates both requestAsset (131-134) and animatedModel (218-220), so assetTemplateDidLoad's rebuild (GeoARSessionManager.swift:1701-1721) runs exactly once per failed decode and the rebuilt entity never re-requests — no loop, no placeholder flicker, and the loadAsync .failure is now logged (DropEntityFactory.swift:88-90).

ARP-3 normal path is fixed: farMode short-circuits on geospatial.semanticActive first (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2099-2103), so the 15-55 m band that latched the flag now clears it. Per-frame cost is LOWER than before the fix — the placedHolders distance scan only runs when semantics are on, and semanticFeed.setEnabled is a single uncontended NSLock write (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:27-31).

persistErrorText's auto-clear cannot be raced into erasing a newer message: showPersistError cancels the previous timer before installing the new one and the timer re-checks Task.isCancelled after the sleep (GeoARSessionManager.swift:87-95); both run as main-actor jobs, so a superseded timer that already woke still returns without clobbering.

Generation guarding holds: a superseded performCloudSync suspended in Firestore's offline continuation cannot clear pending, report an outcome, or unregister its successor (DropStore.swift:356-358, 363-364, 371-372, 374-375); remove() bumps the generation before clearing so an in-flight save cannot resurrect the pending flag (DropStore.swift:296-299).

Delete path is sound in the shipped rules: remove() writes disk first and keeps the row + pending flag intact on failure (DropStore.swift:288-295), skips cloud deletes for received drops (304), and the accepted tombstone-clearing path (392-397) cannot resurrect a row, because FirebaseDropStore.loadDrops is scoped to whereField("ownerUid", isEqualTo: uid) and the only deletes README rules v2 denies are of docs that were never uploaded.

CreateWizard's phantom-drop path is closed: place() opens the share moment only after a successful disk write and otherwise raises a modal alert (CreateWizard.swift:636-648, 93-105); ProfileScreen's chip order (error -> pending -> synced) is honest and now derived from acknowledged writes (ProfileScreen.swift:71-96).

LocalDropStore's actor migration + failable per-row decode + digest-named sidecars behave as claimed: rows decode individually, id-less rows are quarantined rather than re-minted, repeat loads of identical bad bytes do not accumulate sidecars, and save/delete rethrow instead of collapsing a failed read to [] and erasing the library (DropStore.swift:41-152).

findings.claim: The in-AR surface for a failed 3D-model decode is unreachable on the dominant launch path: DropEntityFactory.preloadAnimatedAssets() runs ~10 s after app configure, but onAssetLoaded is installed only by GeoARSessionManager.attach(), which happens on camera intent. Failures recorded during preload therefore fire onAssetLoaded?(name,false) into a nil handler, populate the negative cache silently, and render a permanent "3D?" marker with no message anywhere in the app, ever.
findings.evidence: ARSessionHolder.configure schedules the preload on a 10 s delay (ARSessionHolder.swift:34-37); attach — the only installer of the callback — runs from startIfNeeded(), reached solely via cameraDidAppear()/beginRevealWarmup() (ARSessionHolder.swift:94-107, GeoARSessionManager.swift:321-326). preloadAnimatedAssets inserts into failedAssets and then calls the OPTIONAL handler (DropEntityFactory.swift:120-123). Thereafter animatedModel returns text("3D?") for that name forever and deliberately does not re-request (DropEntityFactory.swift:218-220); failedAssets is never cleared and is exposed nowhere else (only reads are lines 134 and 218). The only other surface, persistErrorText, is a 4 s transient rendered inside hudOverlay, itself gated on !hudHidden and on the AR cover being presented (ARScreen.swift:143-146, 406-412).
findings.failureScenario: A bundled .usdz is corrupt or exported in a flavor this OS build can't decode. First launch: the user is in onboarding/on the map for more than 10 s, so the preload runs with onAssetLoaded == nil — no toast, no rebuild, no user-visible trace. The user then walks to a drop that uses that asset (or picks it from the Playground menu, which still lists it — ARScreen.swift:307-313) and sees a grey "3D?" block where their gift should be, on every launch, with nothing in the UI explaining it. Wave C's C19/C20 promise ("the user is told in-AR") is delivered only in the narrow window where the camera was opened within 10 s of launch.
findings.proposedFix: Make the failure durable and render-time, not decode-time: expose the negative cache (e.g. `static var failedAssetNames: Set<String>`), have animatedModel report the marker it just emitted back to the session manager, and surface a sticky in-AR message ("Kevin's model couldn't be loaded") for as long as a placed drop is rendering the "3D?" marker, instead of a 4 s toast. In attach(), replay any failures already in the cache so decodes that finished before the handler existed are still reported.

findings.claim: The share CTA's caption chain never consults library.lastSyncError, so a terminally rejected upload reads as success at the exact place SWE-3 demanded honesty: after DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount the pending flag is cleared, and the sheet falls through to "Sharing makes this drop visible to anyone with the link" for a drop the server will never accept.
findings.evidence: The caption is a three-way chain — local shareError, else pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id), else the cheerful default (ShareDropSheet.swift:130-146); library.lastSyncError is never read in this file. performCloudSync's terminal branch does clearPending(drop.id) and sets only lastSyncError (DropStore.swift:371-373), so the pending branch stops matching and the else branch wins. For a non-terminal rejection (rules denial) the drop stays pending and the caption says "Still uploading — the link starts working once your drop reaches the cloud" indefinitely (DropStore.swift:375-376 vs ShareDropSheet.swift:135-141). sendLink() presents the system share sheet on LOCAL persistence success alone, and that sheet dismisses the whole ShareDropSheet on completion (ShareDropSheet.swift:151, 165-172), so the honest pending caption is covered at the one moment it matters.
findings.failureScenario: A user restores to a new device (or loses the keychain entry) so Firebase mints a fresh anonymous UID while drops.json, restored from backup, still carries the old ownerUid. They open a drop from Sent, tap "Send the magic link", and the iOS share sheet appears; they text the link. The cloud write throws ownedByAnotherAccount, pending is cleared, and re-opening the sheet shows "Sharing makes this drop visible to anyone with the link" — a statement the app knows to be false. The recipient gets "This drop isn't available". This is the original SWE-3 dead link, now accompanied by an explicit false claim at the CTA.
findings.proposedFix: Extract the caption into a pure state function (shareState(shareError:pending:syncError:)) with a fourth `.failed(String)` case fed by library.lastSyncError, and have it win over both pending and default. Keep the ShareDropSheet alive after the activity sheet is dismissed (drop the onDismiss: dismiss()) until the drop leaves pendingSyncIDs, so the user sees the upload resolve or fail; on a terminal error offer a retry rather than a link.

findings.claim: Failures routed to library.lastPersistError are invisible from the two screens that trigger them: the receive flow swallows the write error with try? and immediately presents the AR cover (which renders only manager.persistErrorText), and the map's Remove-drop action does the same on a screen that has no banner at all. The Sent tab is the only renderer of lastPersistError and is behind a full-screen cover in the receive case.
findings.evidence: RootView.swift:56-61 — `Task { try? await library.update(drop, persist: true) }` with the comment "Failure is published via library.lastPersistError", followed synchronously by reactionSession.startWatching(drop) and router.showCamera = true. lastPersistError is read in exactly one place, DropsListScreen.swift:44-48. The AR HUD renders only manager.persistErrorText (ARScreen.swift:406-412). DropLibrary.update applies the in-memory mutation BEFORE the throwing disk write (DropStore.swift:269-284), so the drop is present and rendered even though it never reached disk. MapScreen.swift:36 has the same `try? await library.remove(drop)` with no banner on that screen.
findings.failureScenario: Storage is full (or the container is momentarily unwritable). A friend's magic link opens the invitation; the user taps through, the local save throws, is swallowed, and they are dropped straight into the camera with the received drop rendering. They watch it, react, and get the Memory screen. Nothing anywhere tells them the drop was never saved; on the next launch it is simply gone from Home's "received" section (HomeScreen.swift:54). The same class on the map: Remove drop fails, the pin stays put with no message, and the user taps it again.
findings.proposedFix: Await the update in the receive callback and, on failure, either block the transition with an alert or push the message into the manager's in-AR channel (manager.showPersistError) before setting router.showCamera. For MapScreen, surface lastPersistError on the map (same banner component as DropsListScreen) or show a local alert at the delete site. As a systemic backstop, render lastPersistError once at RootView level (overlay) rather than on a single tab.

findings.claim: ARP-3's flag can still stick: farMode is computed in frameUpdate(), which returns before that code whenever the session is interrupted, failed, or not in gpsCompass mode — while the consumer of the flag, updatePowerTier()'s passNeeded/detach decision, is skipped by the same conditions. So an interruption freezes semanticMatteArmed at true, leaves the Metal post-process callbacks attached, and keeps the purple SEM chip lit while Google's NN is off.
findings.evidence: frameUpdate guards `mode == .gpsCompass, let arView, !isInterrupted, !sessionFailed` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2018-2019) ahead of the farMode block (2095-2108); tick() — the only caller of updatePowerTier and hence of the 5 s idle detach — guards on the same flags (886-890, 1037-1048). The flag is never cleared anywhere else (only writes are 2105-2106), and neither suspendSession (372-383) nor detach (352-368, which nils semanticPass while frameUpdate's block is `if semanticPass != nil`) resets it. frameUpdate's own comment concedes that "RealityKit keeps rendering (and firing SceneEvents) on a frozen or dead camera" (2015-2017), so the attached pass keeps paying its full-screen copy per rendered frame throughout.
findings.failureScenario: A user is walking to a drop 80 m away; semantics arm, the pass attaches, SEM lights. A phone call arrives: sessionWasInterrupted sets isInterrupted (2276-2283) while the app stays foreground and RealityKit keeps rendering. For the whole call, frameUpdate and tick both bail, semanticMatteArmed stays true, the offscreen-render + blit runs every frame on a frozen camera, and the HUD still claims the semantic matte is armed — ADR-035's exact heat regression, reached through the one input combination the fix left uncovered. The same freeze holds after session(_:didFailWithError:) until the deferred 5 s recovery fires (2299-2328).
findings.proposedFix: Compute the flag where it is consumed, or clear it on the way into the guarded states. Concretely: extract a pure `farModeDecision(sessionLive:semanticActive:thermalSerious:tier:anyHolderBeyond:)` and call it from updatePowerTier (which already scans placedHolders distances at 962-975), passing sessionLive = !isInterrupted && !sessionFailed && mode == .gpsCompass; and set semanticMatteArmed = false + semanticFeed.setEnabled(false) in sessionWasInterrupted, didFailWithError, suspendSession and detach.

soundAreas: LocalDropStore actor conversion (SWE-8) is correct: save/delete are load-modify-write inside the actor, persist() is atomic, and the C5 amendment genuinely rethrows instead of collapsing a failed read to [] — DropStore.swift:139/146. testConcurrentSavesAllSurvive pins it.

Per-row failable decode (SWE-9/C9) is sound: FailableDrop requires a decodable `id` before accepting a row (DropStore.swift:74-79), so id-less rows are quarantined rather than duplicated; the SHA256-digest sidecar name (DropStore.swift:122-129) dedupes repeated loads of identical bad bytes without suppressing genuinely new corruption.

ARP-3 is genuinely closed for every shipping session: farMode/semanticMatteArmed are now computed unconditionally under `if semanticPass != nil` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2095-2107), so the flag falls and geospatial.semanticFeed.setEnabled(false) runs. Latent coupling worth noting but not a defect today: the block lives in frameUpdate(), which early-returns unless `mode == .gpsCompass` (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2018) — the flag would re-latch on a gpsCompass→geoTracking transition, but AppConfig.appleGeoAnchorsEnabled is false (AppConfig.swift:22) so runGeoTracking() is unreachable.

SWE-6 negative asset cache holds: failedAssets gates requestAsset (DropEntityFactory.swift:132-134) AND animatedModel's re-request (DropEntityFactory.swift:216-219), closing the loop at both ends. preloadAnimatedAssets does not filter failedAssets (DropEntityFactory.swift:108-111), but ARSessionHolder.configure is idempotent (`if self.locationService == nil`, ARSessionHolder.swift:26-38) so preload runs once per process — no retry loop in practice.

PBS-7 profile seeding is correct: the seed branch requires !snapshot.exists AND !snapshot.metadata.isFromCache AND profile == nil (AccountService.swift:58-60), includeMetadataChanges:true is on so the server-confirmed-absence event actually arrives, and the C23 branch never seeds over an existing-but-undecodable doc (AccountService.swift:52-57). The obvious residual hole — an offline reinstall leaving profile == nil and the user editing over their real server profile via `profile ?? UserProfile(...)` (AccountService.swift:124) — is closed because ProfileScreen's Edit button is `.disabled(account.profile == nil)` (ProfileScreen.swift:45).

remove()'s disk-first ordering (C26) is right — local.delete throws before any bookkeeping is destroyed (DropStore.swift:290-296) — and the received-drop guard (DropStore.swift:304) plus the FirebaseDropStore backstop (FirebaseDropStore.swift:99) mean a recipient deleting a received drop never fires a delete at the sharer's document.

FirebaseDropStore.save's acknowledgement seam is leak-free: the encode throw is caught and resumes the same continuation (FirebaseDropStore.swift:86-89), so there is no path where the continuation is abandoned.

reconcileCloud's push-only loop genuinely fixes C1/C10/C21 — absence from `drops` no longer clears the outbox (DropStore.swift:317-327) — and mutating pendingSyncIDs via markPending while iterating it is safe (Set value semantics).

add()'s disk-before-memory ordering (DropStore.swift:252-262) plus CreateWizard's alert gate (CreateWizard.swift place()) mean the share moment cannot open for a drop that never reached disk. The create leg of SWE-14 is correctly closed.

findings.claim: refresh() has no generation guard and no cancellation check, so a still-in-flight refresh assigns its stale snapshot over `drops` wholesale — resurrecting a drop deleted during the cloud read and erasing a drop created during it. The sync pipeline got meticulous generation guards in round 2 (C2/C22); the read path that actually publishes `drops` got none.
findings.evidence: `func refresh(near:)` builds a local `merged` dictionary from a local read (DropStore.swift:219), awaits `cloud.loadDrops` (DropStore.swift:228), then unconditionally does `drops = merged.values.sorted { $0.createdAt > $1.createdAt }` (DropStore.swift:244). Nothing captures a generation, nothing consults `Task.isCancelled`, and there is no re-read of local state after the await. Three call sites fire it concurrently in normal use: AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:33 (`await dropLibrary.refresh(near:)` in the launch .task), RootView.swift:123 (`.task(id: account.uid ?? "-")`, which re-fires the moment anonymous sign-in lands), and MapScreen.swift:105-107 (`.task(id: locationService.location == nil)`). SwiftUI cancels MapScreen's task on tab switch, but Firestore's `getDocuments()` bridge is not cancellation-aware — the continuation still resumes and the body runs on past the await to line 244. Meanwhile `remove()` (DropStore.swift:286-307) and `add()` (DropStore.swift:252-263) mutate `drops` on the main actor in the gap.
findings.failureScenario: User is on Explore; MapScreen's .task fires refresh with a real location and the Firestore read stalls on a weak network. The user switches to Sent and swipe-deletes drop D: local.delete succeeds, D leaves `drops` and leaves drops.json, the tombstone is written and the cloud delete is queued. The stalled cloud read then resumes with a snapshot that predates all of it, and line 244 replaces `drops` with the stale merge — D is back in the Sent list and back in the AR renderer. The user opens D in the camera and nudges the height slider: GeoARSessionManager's commit calls `library.update(D, persist: true)`, which writes D back to drops.json (DropStore.swift:277) and calls `enqueueCloudSync(D)` (DropStore.swift:283), re-uploading the document the tombstone just deleted. The delete is permanently undone. The mirror case is equally real: a drop created during the same window is absent from the stale snapshot and vanishes from Sent/Home/AR immediately after the create ritual — the exact 'freshly created drop vanishing' symptom SWE-8 was written to kill, reintroduced one layer up.
findings.proposedFix: Give refresh() the same generation discipline the sync pipeline has: bump a `refreshGeneration` at entry, capture it, and after every await `guard refreshGeneration == captured else { return }` before touching `drops`, `lastSyncError` or `localReadWarning`. Additionally re-read the local store after the cloud await (or merge into the CURRENT `drops` rather than into a pre-await snapshot) so mutations committed during the read are never overwritten, and add `guard !Task.isCancelled` after the cloud read.

testCase.name: testInFlightRefreshCannotResurrectADropDeletedDuringIt

Build DropLibrary(localStore:cloudStore:). `try await library.add(d)`; wait for the ack so pendingSyncIDs is empty. Act: `let refreshTask = Task { await library.refresh(near: nil) }`; await `enteredLoad`; `try await library.remove(d)`; release the gate; `await refreshTask.value`. Assert: `XCTAssertFalse(library.drops.contains { $0.id == d.id })` and `XCTAssertTrue(try await LocalDropStore(fileURL: url).loadDrops(near: nil, radius: 0).isEmpty)`. Second act/assert in the same test for the mirror case: repeat with `try await library.add(e)` inside the gate instead of remove, and assert `library.drops.contains { $0.id == e.id }`.

findings.claim: The whole-file-corruption warning is destroyed by the very next refresh, so a total library loss IS silent — the exact failure C7 was written to close. The quarantine moves drops.json away; the next load sees no file and sets `pendingReadWarning = nil`; the library's banner is recomputed from that and goes blank. The app fires two refreshes back-to-back at launch, so the warning is erased before a user can possibly reach the Sent tab.
findings.evidence: loadDrops's missing-file path unconditionally clears the verdict: `guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) else { pendingReadWarning = nil; return [] }` (DropStore.swift:84-87). The corruption path moves the file away — `try? FileManager.default.moveItem(at: fileURL, to: quarantine)` (DropStore.swift:111) — and sets the warning (DropStore.swift:113). refresh() then mirrors whatever the LAST load said, including nil: `localReadWarning = await localStore.lastLoadReadWarning()` (DropStore.swift:222-225), and DropsListScreen renders the banner only `if let warning = library.localReadWarning` (DropsListScreen.swift:49). The launch sequence guarantees two loads: AugmentMeRealityApp.swift:33 runs `await dropLibrary.refresh(near:)` in the app .task, and RootView.swift:121-124's `.task(id: account.uid ?? "-")` re-fires and calls `refresh(near: nil)` as soon as anonymous sign-in resolves (typically well under two seconds). The same three lines hide a second silent-empty path: refresh() reads the local store with `try?` (DropStore.swift:219), and a throw from `let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)` (DropStore.swift:88) sits OUTSIDE the do/catch, so it leaves pendingReadWarning at its stale previous value while contributing zero drops.
findings.failureScenario: A user's drops.json is left non-JSON (partial restore from backup, an interrupted external write, filesystem damage). Launch: refresh #1 quarantines the file to drops.json.corrupt-1755264000 and sets localReadWarning. Sign-in completes ~1s later; refresh #2 finds no drops.json, nils pendingReadWarning, and nils localReadWarning. The user opens Sent and sees ContentUnavailableView 'No drops yet — Pin your first 3D surprise…' (DropsListScreen.swift:67-71) with no banner of any kind. Every drop they ever made is gone, the only copy is an invisible sibling file, and the app's cheerful empty state tells them this is a fresh install. DropStoreTests.testCorruptFileIsQuarantinedAndReplaced asserts the warning at exactly the one moment it exists — immediately after the single load — and never models the second load that erases it.
findings.proposedFix: Make the destructive verdict sticky rather than derived from the last load: persist a quarantine record (e.g. the quarantine filename in UserDefaults, or a `quarantinedAt` field on the store) that loadDrops does NOT clear on a missing file, and have refresh() OR it with the transient skipped-rows warning. Clear it only on an explicit user acknowledgement or once a non-empty library exists again. Separately, wrap `Data(contentsOf:)` so a read throw also sets a warning before propagating, and stop swallowing that throw with `try?` at DropStore.swift:219.

findings.claim: After a terminal cloud-sync failure the share sheet reverts to its most reassuring copy. `performCloudSync` clears the pending flag on DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount (round-2 C4/C15), which is the ONLY per-drop signal ShareDropSheet consults — so the honest gold 'Still uploading' hint flips back to 'Sharing makes this drop visible to anyone with the link' for a drop whose upload has permanently failed. SWE-3's original failure — a live-looking link that is dead forever and the sender is never told — is reintroduced through the round-2 amendment.
findings.evidence: ShareDropSheet's status line is a three-way branch on `shareError` (local persist only), then `library.pendingSyncIDs.contains(drop.id)`, then the reassuring default at ShareDropSheet.swift:142-146. It never reads `library.lastSyncError`. `performCloudSync`'s terminal branch does `clearPending(drop.id); lastSyncError = DropStoreError.ownedByAnotherAccount.errorDescription` (DropStore.swift:368-373) — pending is dropped, and the only surviving evidence is a single global string rendered on the Sent tab (DropsListScreen.swift:39-43) and in Profile (ProfileScreen.swift), neither of which is on screen. `sendLink()` has already set `showShareSheet = true` (ShareDropSheet.swift:171), so UIActivityViewController is presented over the copy the moment the CTA is tapped, and the copy underneath silently changes from gold to reassuring while the user is picking a recipient.
findings.failureScenario: A user restores their phone to a new device: drops.json comes back from the backup carrying ownerUid = the old anonymous UID, but the keychain entry did not survive so Firebase mints a NEW anonymous UID (Theme 12's reinstall case, minus the keychain). The user opens Sent, sees their old drops, taps Share on one, and taps 'Send the magic link'. Local persist succeeds, `enqueueCloudSync` marks it pending, and the sheet honestly reads 'Still uploading — the link starts working once your drop reaches the cloud'. FirebaseDropStore.save then throws .ownedByAnotherAccount (FirebaseDropStore.swift:55-57); pending is cleared; the line under the CTA becomes 'Sharing makes this drop visible to anyone with the link'. The user texts the link. The recipient sees 'This drop isn't available'. Neither party is ever told, and the sender's only clue is an orange banner on a tab they are not on.
findings.proposedFix: Record terminal sync failures per drop, not only in the global `lastSyncError`: add `@Published private(set) var failedSyncIDs: Set<UUID>` (or a `[UUID: String]` of reasons), populate it in the .ownedByAnotherAccount branch alongside clearPending, clear it on the next successful ack, and give ShareDropSheet a fourth branch above the reassuring default that renders the per-drop failure in Night.coral and blocks/labels the CTA. `sendLink()` should also refuse to present the activity sheet when the drop is already in failedSyncIDs.
